Twitch — viewer controls and content labels (official)

twitch.noKidsAlt: Twitch's terms say the service is not available under 13 at all, so there is no younger version to move to.

netflix.name: Netflix
netflix.blurb: A kids profile is easy to make and does very little on its own. What matters is locking the adult profiles, because otherwise your child is two taps away from all of them.
risks: A kids profile is pointless if the adult profiles have no PIN, and profile locks are off by default
Each adult profile has to be locked separately
A Kids profile's rating cannot be raised later, and Netflix's fix is to delete it and lose the history
beforeYouStart: Do this on a computer or in the mobile app. Most of it cannot be done from the TV app.
You'll need your Netflix password a few times.

steps.title: Make them their own profile
steps.why: Ratings, autoplay and history are all set per profile, so a shared profile means none of it applies.
steps.path: Manage Profiles → Add Profile → For Kids
do: Open Manage Profiles, then Add Profile.
Name it, and tick the For Kids box for younger children.
On a TV the label may read Kids Profile rather than For Kids.
steps.note: The main account profile cannot be turned into a kids profile, and there is a limit of five profiles.

steps.title: Set the maturity rating
steps.why: This is the main content control, and it applies to Netflix games as well as films and shows.
do: Go to Account, then Profiles, then Adjust parental controls.
Pick the profile and verify it's you.
Set the maturity rating and save.
steps.note: Rating names vary by country. These are the US names; in the UK and Ireland you'll see BBFC ratings in the same place.

steps.title: Lock every adult profile with a PIN
steps.why: This is the step almost everyone misses, and without it the rest is decoration. A child who can tap back to your profile has no restrictions at all.
do: Go to Account, then Profiles, then pick an adult profile.
Choose Profile Lock, then Create a Profile Lock.
Set a 4-digit PIN and save.
Repeat for every adult profile on the account.
steps.result: Your child can no longer switch into an unrestricted profile.
steps.note: On the main profile you can also turn on Require a PIN to add a new profile, which stops them making a fresh unrestricted one. Note that Extra Member accounts cannot use profile locks at all.

steps.title: Block specific titles if you need to
steps.why: Netflix is the only one of the big streamers that lets you block an individual show.
steps.path: Account → Profiles → Adjust parental controls → Title Restrictions
do: On the same parental controls screen, find Title Restrictions.
Type the title and select it.
Save.

steps.title: Turn off autoplay
steps.why: Autoplay is what turns one episode into an evening, and previews are what surface things they weren't looking for.
do: Go to Account, then Profiles, then the child's profile, then Playback settings.
Turn off Autoplay previews and Autoplay next episode.

steps.title: Add a device-level backstop
steps.why: These settings only cover this one service. A device-level control catches the app they download next.
do: Set up Screen Time, Family Link, Microsoft Family Safety or your console's own controls.
Require your approval for new app downloads.
steps.note: SafeStart has a separate guide for each of these. Pick your device on the home screen.

checklist: Maturity rating set for their age
Every adult profile has a PIN
talkAboutIt: Watch the first episode of something new with them rather than vetting it alone.
Agree what they do if something they start makes them uncomfortable: stop it and tell you.

links.label: Netflix — maturity ratings and blocking titles (official)

kidsAlt.name: A Kids profile
kidsAlt.what: Tick “For Kids” when you add a profile. It has a simpler layout, blocks access to account settings, and has no email of its own, so nobody can sign in with it directly.
kidsAlt.watchOut: Setting a maturity rating above the kids level quietly switches the kid-safe features off. Put a profile lock PIN on your own profile too, or they will just tap across to it.

disneyplus.name: Disney+
disneyplus.blurb: Junior Mode is a solid walled garden for young children. The setting that catches people out is the one allowing unrated live sports and news, which is on by default and includes its ad breaks.
risks: Unrated live content is allowed by default on every profile that isn't in Junior Mode
The main profile defaults to the highest rating and cannot be put in Junior Mode
Junior Mode is all or nothing, with no middle setting for an older child
beforeYouStart: You can only change these on a web browser or in the mobile app, not on the TV app.
Have your Disney+ password ready. Most of these steps ask for it.

steps.title: Turn on Junior Mode for younger children
steps.why: This is the kids profile, renamed. If you go looking for Kids Profile in the app you won't find it.
steps.path: Edit Profiles → [profile] → Parental Controls → Junior Mode
do: Go to your profiles and choose Add Profile, or Edit Profiles for one that exists.
Pick an avatar and name it.
Under Parental Controls, switch Junior Mode on.
Save.
steps.note: Junior Mode profiles see no ads. The main profile cannot be put into Junior Mode, and turning Junior Mode off needs your password.

steps.title: Set the content rating for an older child
steps.why: For a child too old for the all-ages walled garden, the rating is the only content lever, because Junior Mode cannot be tuned.
steps.path: Edit Profiles → [profile] → Parental Controls → Content rating
do: Go to your profiles, choose Edit Profiles, and select the profile.
Under Parental Controls choose Content rating.
Enter your password, pick the rating, and save.
steps.note: Rating names vary by country. These are the US names; in the UK and Ireland you'll see BBFC ratings in the same place.

steps.title: Turn off unrated live content
steps.why: This is the one that catches people out. It is on by default, and Disney's own warning is blunt: live content and live ads may feature adult themes, products and services. Setting a child's profile to a low rating and stopping there leaves live sports, live news and their ad breaks wide open.
steps.path: Edit Profiles → [profile] → Parental Controls → allow titles without ratings
do: On the same Parental Controls screen for the profile, find the setting allowing titles without ratings, such as live sports and news.
Turn it off.
steps.result: Unrated live content and its ads no longer appear on that profile.
steps.note: Turning it back on later needs your password. Turning it off does not.

steps.title: Put a PIN on your own profile
steps.why: The main profile defaults to the highest rating, so without a PIN your child switches into it in two taps.
steps.path: Edit Profiles → [your profile] → Parental Controls → Profile PIN
do: Go to your profiles, choose Edit Profiles, and select your own profile.
Under Parental Controls choose Profile PIN.
Enter your password, set a 4-digit PIN, and save.
steps.result: Your profile can no longer be opened without the PIN.

steps.title: Stop new profiles being created
steps.why: Otherwise a child simply makes themselves a fresh unrestricted one.
do: Open Account.
Under Settings, turn Restrict profile creation on.
Enter your password and continue.

steps.title: Turn on Kid-Proof Exit
steps.why: Makes leaving Junior Mode deliberate rather than accidental.
do: Go to Edit Profiles and switch Kid-Proof Exit on.
Enter your password.
steps.note: This only slows the exit from Junior Mode. It does not lock where they land, which is what the profile PIN above is for.

steps.title: Add a device-level backstop
steps.why: These settings only cover this one service. A device-level control catches the app they download next.
do: Set up Screen Time, Family Link, Microsoft Family Safety or your console's own controls.
Require your approval for new app downloads.
steps.note: SafeStart has a separate guide for each of these. Pick your device on the home screen.

checklist: Junior Mode on, or a content rating set
Kid-Proof Exit on for younger children
talkAboutIt: Junior Mode is all-ages, so an older child will find it babyish. Better to talk about why than let them work around it.
Agree what they do if something they start makes them uncomfortable.

kidsAlt.name: Junior Mode
kidsAlt.what: A simpler profile that only shows content suitable for all ages. The ceiling is fixed, so there is no rating to adjust and nothing to get wrong.
kidsAlt.watchOut: Kid-Proof Exit is a challenge, not a lock, so add a profile PIN to the adult profiles as well. Parents of 10 to 12 year olds often find Junior Mode too limited and switch it off, which leaves nothing in its place.

primevideo.name: Prime Video
primevideo.blurb: The controls are good, but two things trip parents up: viewing restrictions apply only to the device you set them on, and downloads from your profile stay visible in a kids profile.
risks: Viewing restrictions apply per device, so setting them on the laptop does nothing to the TV or tablet
Downloads made on an adult profile are still reachable from a kids profile
Setting the PIN does not by itself switch the restrictions on
beforeYouStart: Have your Amazon account password ready.
Make a list of every device the household watches on. You will need to repeat one step on each.

steps.title: Create the Account PIN
steps.why: This one PIN sits above everything. It locks purchases, overrides any profile PIN, and controls who can add or remove profiles.
steps.path: Your Profiles → Edit profile → Account PIN and locks
do: Go to Your Profiles, then Edit profile, and pick the account holder's profile.
Choose Manage next to Account PIN and locks.
Enter your Amazon details.
Choose Create next to Prime Video Account PIN, set it, and continue.
steps.note: Creating the PIN is not the same as switching restrictions on. On Android in particular they are two separate actions, so do the next steps as well.

steps.title: Make them a kids profile
steps.why: A kids profile only shows titles rated 12 and under, filters search, and blocks purchases outright.
do: Hover over your profile icon and choose Add new, or use Edit profiles on mobile.
Name it and set it up as a kids profile.
You can have up to six profiles in total.
steps.note: Be aware of one real hole: downloads made on an adult profile, including an 18-rated film, stay accessible from the kids profile.

steps.title: Set viewing restrictions, then repeat on every device
steps.why: This is the trap. Prime Video's own help pages say it plainly: viewing restrictions only apply to the device that set them up. The settings screen does not look like that.
do: On a computer, go to Account & Settings, then Permissions.
Choose the age restriction and tick the devices you want it to apply to.
Save.
Now do the same on the TV, the tablet and any phone they watch on.

recommended.16-17: Young Adults (16+), or agree it together

steps.result: Only content at or below that level plays on the devices you ticked.
steps.note: The five levels are Kids (All), Older Kids (7+), Teens (13+), Young Adults (16+) and Adults (18+). They map to local ratings, so in the UK and Ireland they line up with U, PG, 12, 15 and 18.

steps.title: Lock purchases
steps.why: Rentals and purchases are one tap from the same screen they watch on.
do: From the same Permissions screen, turn on purchase restrictions.
On Android this lives under Settings, then Parental Controls, then Purchase Restrictions.
steps.result: Buying or renting now needs your Account PIN.
steps.note: Purchase restrictions do apply to every profile and every device, unlike viewing restrictions.

steps.title: Lock your own profile and stop new ones
steps.why: Otherwise your child watches from your profile instead of theirs.
steps.path: Your Profiles → Edit profile → Profile / Account PIN and locks
do: Go to Your Profiles, Edit profile, then your own profile.
Choose Manage next to Profile / Account PIN and locks, enter your password and PIN.
Switch Profile lock on and save.
On the same screen, switch Creation and removal lock on.

steps.title: If you watch on a Fire TV, set that separately
steps.why: Fire TV has its own parental controls, and nothing in Prime Video's settings covers them.
do: On the Fire TV device itself, open Settings, then Preferences, then Parental Controls.
Turn them on and set a PIN.
steps.note: Amazon states this outright: Fire TV parental controls have to be managed on the device.

steps.title: Add a device-level backstop
steps.why: These settings only cover this one service. A device-level control catches the app they download next.
do: Set up Screen Time, Family Link, Microsoft Family Safety or your console's own controls.
Require your approval for new app downloads.
steps.note: SafeStart has a separate guide for each of these. Pick your device on the home screen.

checklist: Viewing restrictions set on every device
Fire TV set separately if you have one
talkAboutIt: Explain that downloads on your profile are visible to them, so it is worth agreeing what gets downloaded.
Watch something new together rather than vetting it alone.

links.label: Prime Video — maturity ratings by country (official)

kidsAlt.name: A Kids profile
kidsAlt.form: a profile setting in Prime Video
kidsAlt.what: Shows only content rated 12 and under, filters search results and suggestions, and blocks purchases.
kidsAlt.watchOut: Downloads leak through. Anything downloaded on an adult profile can still be reached from the Kids profile, so PIN-lock the adult profiles too.
